hubDescription: Tree service in Springfield, TN and Robertson County: tree removal, trimming, stump grinding, storm cleanup and land clearing. Licensed, insured, free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
hubIntro: Springfield was founded in 1819 and is the Robertson County seat, about thirty miles north of downtown Nashville. Its Town Square Historic District, a four-block area of thirty-four historic buildings around the Robertson County Courthouse, anchors the older part of the city, and the surrounding blocks are lined with established shade trees. Farm country, including the dark-fired tobacco land the area is known for, begins just past the edge of town.

Triple Oak Services is based in Nashville and travels to Springfield for tree removal, tree trimming and pruning, stump grinding, storm damage cleanup and land clearing. This page covers what tree work in Springfield tends to involve, how its old streets and farm edges shape the work, and what to know before you hire a crew. Every job starts with a free, no-obligation estimate.

sections.h2: Around the Town Square and the older streets
paragraphs: The blocks around Springfield's Town Square, 6th Avenue West and the older residential streets nearby are among the oldest in the county, and the trees in them are old too. Large oaks, maples and hackberries stand beside houses and brick buildings from the 1800s, and their crowns often reach across roofs, porches and overhead lines. Tight lots, old fences and narrow access make most work here close-quarters, with trees taken down in sections and cleanup done with care.

Owners of older properties often want a tree preserved rather than removed, and we are glad to look at crown cleaning, thinning and hazard reduction first. When a tree is dead, diseased or leaning toward a building, we explain the safest way to take it down and what the job includes.

sections.h2: Highway 41, newer subdivisions and the edge of town
paragraphs: Springfield has grown along Highway 41 (Dixie Highway) and Highway 76, and newer subdivisions now sit beside older farmland. Builders often plant fast-growing trees close to foundations and driveways, and trees saved from the original lots can decline after their roots are damaged in construction. Tree lines along property edges have often never been thinned, and dead trees mixed in with healthy ones are easy to miss until a storm brings them down.

Larger lots near the edge of town bring bigger jobs: windbreaks and fence-line trees, cedars and hackberries along back property lines and brush that needs clearing before a pool, shop or driveway goes in. Those calls often combine removal, stump grinding and land clearing in one visit.

sections.h2: Tobacco country, open land and storm exposure
paragraphs: Springfield is surrounded by farmland, including the dark-fired tobacco ground that earned the area its reputation. Open land gives wind room to build, so trees on exposed field edges, ridgelines and the outskirts of town take the full force of spring thunderstorms and straight-line winds. Saturated soil after heavy rain loosens roots, and summer drought leaves trees with dead limbs that drop in later storms.

Warning signs worth watching include a lean that is getting worse, cracks in the trunk or where a big limb meets it, mushrooms or conks around the base, soil heaving on one side and large dead branches in the crown. Any of them is a reason to have the tree inspected before the next storm.

sections.h2: Before you remove a tree in Springfield
paragraphs: Whether you need approval depends on the property. Rules can vary depending on whether you are inside the city or in unincorporated Robertson County, whether the property lies in or near a historic district, and whether an HOA applies. Street trees and trees in the public right-of-way cannot be removed by a homeowner or contractor. Check with the City of Springfield and your HOA before removing a large tree, and confirm current requirements, since rules can change.

Look up before work begins. Trees touching or close to power lines should be handled by the utility or a qualified line-clearance crew, and anyone in danger should call 911. If stump grinding or digging is involved, call Tennessee 811 so buried utilities are marked. We point out lines, fences, septic fields and structures when we quote.

We are a locally owned, licensed and insured company. For Springfield jobs we give a free estimate, explain how the tree will come down and what the price includes, remove it safely and haul the debris away. Stump grinding and brush clearing can be added on the same visit, and storm damage and emergency removal are available when a tree is already down. If trimming will do the job, we will tell you.

tree-trimming-pruning.title: Tree Trimming & Pruning in Springfield, TN | Triple Oak Services
tree-trimming-pruning.description: Tree trimming and pruning in Springfield, TN: dead limb removal, crown thinning, clearance from roofs and lines, storm-risk reduction. Licensed, insured. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: The old shade trees around Springfield's Town Square and older streets are worth keeping, and regular pruning is how they last. Removing dead wood, thinning heavy crowns and shortening overextended limbs lowers the chance of a branch failing over a roof, car or sidewalk.

In newer parts of town along Highway 41 and Highway 76, trimming is often about clearance: limbs off roofs and siding, branches away from service lines and young trees shaped early so they grow strong. On larger lots, overgrown tree lines can be thinned so they stop shading and crowding fences.
We do not top trees. We explain what will be removed and why before any cutting begins.

faq.q: Can you prune old trees near historic buildings?
faq.a: Yes. Careful crown cleaning and selective thinning are common on older trees, and we explain the plan before cutting.

faq.q: How often should trees be trimmed?
faq.a: Many mature trees benefit from a check every few years. Dead wood and limbs over structures should be handled as soon as you notice them.

stump-grinding.title: Stump Grinding in Springfield, TN | Triple Oak Services
stump-grinding.description: Stump grinding in Springfield, TN: stumps ground below grade, root flare removal and cleanup so your yard is ready to use. Free estimates. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: A stump holds moisture, attracts insects and fungus and makes mowing and landscaping harder. We grind stumps below grade in Springfield so the spot can be filled and planted, from a small stump behind a home near the Square to a large hardwood stump on acreage outside town.

Older properties around downtown can have buried lines, old foundations and long root systems around a stump, so the job gets a look first. Call Tennessee 811 before digging or grinding so buried utilities are marked, and we will go over access, depth and cleanup during the estimate.
Stump grinding pairs well with removal. Ask us to grind the stump on the same visit.

faq.q: Can you grind a stump near an old foundation?
faq.a: Often, yes. We look at distance to the foundation, lines and fences during the estimate and plan the work around them.
Chips are cleaned up as part of the job. Tell us if you would like to keep them.

storm-damage-cleanup.description: Storm damage tree cleanup in Springfield, TN: fallen trees, hanging limbs and emergency removal, including same-day service when available. Call 615-561-0472.
paragraphs: Storms reach Springfield across open farmland, and trees on exposed field edges and the outskirts of town take the worst of it. Older shade trees near the Square can lose limbs onto roofs and cars, and fallen trees often block driveways and roads.

If a tree is down, make everyone safe first. If a power line is involved or anyone is in danger, call 911 and your utility, then call us. We provide storm damage and emergency tree removal, including same-day emergency removal where scheduling allows, and we clear trees and limbs from roofs, yards and driveways.
After a storm, check the trees that stayed standing for cracks, loosened soil and hanging branches, and have them looked at before the next one.

If clearing is part of a build, check with the City of Springfield or Robertson County about any permits or approvals. We clear to the lines you mark.
